title: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic RL
hook: Outcome-only RL tells an agent it failed but not which move was the mistake. OPID mines that lesson from the agent's own finished trajectories — turning hindsight into dense, per-token supervision.
key_points: Outcome-based RL gives sparse trajectory-level rewards — little signal about which intermediate decisions to reinforce or suppress.
OPID extracts skill supervision directly from completed on-policy trajectories, avoiding external skill memories or retrieved privileged context.
It represents hindsight as hierarchical skills: episode-level (global workflows, failure-avoidance) and step-level (critical local decisions).
A critical-first router uses step-level skills at key timesteps and falls back to episode-level guidance otherwise.
Re-scoring a response with vs. without the injected skill yields a token-level self-distillation advantage, combined with the outcome advantage.
Improves performance, sample efficiency, and robustness on ALFWorld, WebShop, and search-based QA.
content_html: Reinforcement learning is a stable way to train language agents, but a sparse end-of-episode reward is a blunt teacher: it says the run failed without saying which of dozens of moves was the mistake. OPID (On-Policy Skill Distillation) recovers that fine-grained lesson from the agent's own behavior.
extra_html:
The idea

Rather than reaching for external skill libraries or retrieved expert context — costly to maintain and often mismatched to what the current policy actually does — OPID reads hindsight straight off completed on-policy trajectories. It represents that hindsight as hierarchical skills: episode-level skills capture global workflows or failure-avoidance rules, while step-level skills capture local decision knowledge at critical timesteps. A critical-first router applies step-level skills when a decision looks pivotal and otherwise defaults to episode-level guidance.

How the signal is built

The selected skill is injected into the interaction history, and the old policy re-scores the same sampled response both with and without it. The log-probability shift between those two scorings becomes a token-level self-distillation advantage, which is added to the usual outcome advantage. RL stays the primary objective; the distillation term just supplies dense, distribution-matched supervision. On ALFWorld, WebShop, and search-based QA, the authors report gains in performance, sample efficiency, and robustness over outcome-only RL and prior skill-distillation baselines. Code is linked from the paper.

related.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation isn't a midpoint between fine-tuning and RL — it carves its own narrow path through parameter space, locking into a low-dimensional subspace early in training.

related.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation breaks when teacher and student disagree too much. TrOPD only trusts the teacher where its supervision is reliable — and skips the rest.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

flashcards.prompt: What problem with outcome-based RL for agents does OPID address?
flashcards.back_html: Sparse trajectory-level rewards give little guidance about which intermediate decisions should be reinforced or suppressed. OPID adds dense, token-level supervision derived from the agent's own trajectories.

flashcards.prompt: Where does OPID get its dense supervision signal?

choices.text: From the agent's own completed on-policy trajectories, re-scored with and without an injected hindsight skill
From a large external database of expert demonstrations
From human annotators labeling each step

flashcards.explanation_html: OPID mines hierarchical 'skills' from completed trajectories, injects the relevant one into the history, and uses the resulting log-probability shift as a token-level self-distillation advantage — no external memory needed.

flashcards.prompt: What are the two levels of 'skill' OPID extracts, and how does it choose between them?
flashcards.back_html: Episode-level skills (global workflows, failure-avoidance) and step-level skills (local decisions at critical timesteps). A critical-first router uses step-level skills at key decisions, else falls back to episode-level.
